newsitem.title: UK: EIB considers jumbo mark Eurobond - dealers.
newsitem.headline: EIB considers jumbo mark Eurobond - dealers.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) could launch a Eurobond for up to 1.0 billion marks next week, syndicate managers said on Thursday.
"The EIB is looking at the market and thinking of launching a strategic mark benchmark bond but has not firmed up plans yet," a Frankfurt-based syndicate manager said.
"Flows have been very mixed and the market has been volatile. It is too early to give a firm recommendation to bring a deal," he said.
The EIB was looking at both the five- and 10-year sector, traders said.

The World Bank issued a 500 million mark five-year bond on Wednesday but this was an arbitrage-driven retail-targeted deal and thus would not clash with a more institutional-targeted EIB issue, dealers said.
"There is an Obl 120 auction next week, and the results of this will have an impact on the EIB's decision," a trader at a U.S. bank said.
"We think the 10-year sector looks better than five years because there is no government supply there, in contrast with five years, and a recent Eurofima deal went well," he said.
